citation.title: Mortality and pulmonary mechanics in relation to respiratory system and transpulmonary driving pressures in ARDS

provenance.quote: Patients were included in the study if they had acute lung injury or ARDS as defined by the American–European Consensus Conference [2].

Subjects were monitored while supine with the head of the bed elevated to 30°. An esophageal balloon-catheter was placed, and measurements were obtained to estimate intrathoracic pressures. Airway pressure, tidal volume and air flow were recorded during tidal ventilation.
The EPvent study was approved by the institutional review board at the Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center in Boston.

Patients in the intervention group had PEEP levels adjusted to achieve a positive transpulmonary pressure of 0–10 cm H2O at end-expiration according to a sliding scale based on the fraction of inspired oxygen.
We have examined the relationships between respiratory system and transpulmonary driving pressure, pulmonary mechanics and 28-day mortality.
Data from 29 patients in the control group and 27 patients in the intervention group were analyzed.
Fifty-six patients from a previous study were analyzed to compare PEEP titration to maintain positive transpulmonary end-expiratory pressure to a control protocol.

subgroup_flags.classification_notes: ARDS subgroup: all patients had ALI/ARDS by AECC criteria. Obesity subgroup: BMI not reported. Timing subgroup: intervention timing from intubation not reported; study began at enrollment. PTP target: absolute PEEP-guided PtP range 0-10 cmH2O at end-expiration.

extraction_flags.overlap_evidence: Confirmed overlap with talmor_2008 (EPVent primary report). This paper states: 'Fifty-six patients from a previous study were analyzed' and the original study is EPVent (ref 15). Cohort_id 'epvent1' assigned. Primary report is talmor_2008.
unclear_items: adults_18_plus: age criterion not explicitly stated; adult ICU setting inferred.
